categories.name: Source and analytic universe
categories.definition: Reading the input file and treating its full contents as the analysis population, with no row-level filtering applied at that step.
categories.criterion: if the operation only names/loads the data or declares the whole file the universe (no rows removed) it belongs here, else it is inclusion_exclusion

categories.name: Who stays in the sample
categories.definition: Restricting the analytic sample by dropping rows, subsetting to a group, or gating on a minimum sample size, thereby changing which observations the estimand covers.
categories.criterion: if observations are removed or the population is narrowed it belongs here; if only columns or values are transformed it is variable_construction

categories.name: Building model-ready variables
categories.definition: Deriving, recoding, bucketing, one-hot-encoding, binarizing, restructuring, or selecting the columns that will enter the model, without changing which rows are present.
categories.criterion: if the item produces or reshapes a variable/column set (not a fitted estimator, not a reported number) it belongs here

categories.name: Estimator and specification choices
categories.definition: Fitting or refitting the effect model — its adjustment set, link, clustering, exposure operationalization (cutoff, continuous, extremes), or an alternative outcome family.
categories.criterion: if the operation fits/refits an estimator to produce the effect it belongs here; computing a descriptive quantity from data is estimate_and_summary

categories.name: Descriptive and reported quantities
categories.definition: Computing crude rates, risk differences, balance checks, predicted-probability diagnostics, counterfactual cross-checks, extracted coefficients, or assembling comparison tables of point estimates.
categories.criterion: if the item's point is a computed number/table rather than the interval-or-test formula around it, it belongs here rather than uncertainty_method

categories.name: How uncertainty is derived
categories.definition: Choosing the formula for a standard error, confidence interval, or p-value — Wald 1.96 multipliers, delta method, bootstrap-SE vs bootstrap-tails, or one-sided/z-test derivations.
categories.criterion: if the distinguishing operation is the SE/CI/test formula itself, it belongs here even when a point estimate is computed alongside

categories.name: Silently discarded computations
categories.definition: Quietly discarding bootstrap draws or model fits that fail or fall below a size threshold, without counting or flagging them, corrupting the uncertainty estimate.
categories.criterion: if resampling iterations or fits are dropped without record it belongs here, distinct from inclusion_exclusion which defines the analysis sample

categories.name: Hand-typed numbers in the output
categories.definition: Populating plots or tables with hardcoded literal estimates or CI widths instead of the values actually computed by the run.
categories.criterion: if displayed numbers are not read from the computed result objects it belongs here; choosing how to present genuinely computed numbers is display_framing

categories.name: Presentation framing
categories.definition: Choices that shape what the reader sees of real results — axis limits, truncating shown categories, or curating which computed estimates get featured.
categories.criterion: if the item selects/bounds how correctly-computed results are displayed (not the numbers themselves) it belongs here

result.note: Several items blend two consequences (e.g. 3 is a refit that also silently drops failed draws; 77 both filters and redefines exposure); each is placed by its dominant consequence per the exclusivity rule.
